papers.title_en: OverSeer: Multi-Agent World Models Beyond What Agents See
papers.authors: Runjia Li, Kam Woh Ng, Minghao Chen, Junlin Han, Jianyuan Wang, Zhaochong An, Juan-Manuel Perez-Rua, Andrea Vedaldi, Shikun Liu
papers.evidence: 多智能体视频世界模型，用世界中心辅助视角保持一致性
papers.tldr: 多智能体视频世界模型需生成多个智能体视角，并保持时间与智能体间一致，现有方法难以兼顾。OverSeer在自视角外引入空间固定的辅助相机视角，作为世界中心表征代理，并用delta-VAE仅编码相对静态参考图的变化以压缩冗余。在Minecraft和Doom中，世界与智能体一致性提升，真实多相机定性结果说明不依赖游戏引擎，压缩分析显示辅助视角生成开销显著降低。该工作为多智能体世界模型提供简单高效的一致性增强方案。
papers.abstract_en: Despite the success of video world models, extending them to multiple agents is difficult because it requires generating several agent-specific video streams that are consistent in time and between agents. To address this gap, we introduce OverSeer, a multi-agent world model that augments egocentric agent views with auxiliary camera views. We suggest that, by fixing the auxiliary views in space, they act as a proxy for a world-centric representation: Unlike the agents' views, which can change entirely due to a simple change in agent position, changes in the auxiliary views directly map to localized changes in the world state. We show that these fixed views substantially help the model to maintain consistency. We also show that, due to their redundant and semi-static nature, the auxiliary views can be efficiently compressed with a delta-VAE that encodes only the changes relative to a static reference image, reducing the number of tokens required to process them. Experiments in Minecraft and Doom demonstrate improved world and agent consistency, with qualitative results on real-world multi-camera captures indicating that the approach is not tied to game engines. Our compression analysis further shows that delta-VAE substantially reduces the computational overhead of auxiliary-view generation. We conclude that these fixed views provide a simple and efficient way to improve multi-agent world models.

papers.title_en: $Ψ$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
papers.authors: Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Baihan Zhang, Yifan Liu, Lilian Chen, Atlas Kazemian, Rahul Venkatesh, Daniel Yamins
papers.evidence: 统一视觉语言世界模型，具备多视角空间推理与几何表示
papers.tldr: 现有AI能力常分散在专用模型中，难以按任务灵活组合感知、语言与物理推理。Ψ-0.6以统一视觉-语言世界模型提出“思维流”，在共享token接口中交错生成与解读图像、文本、几何和运动表示。它零样本超越领先开放权重模型的多视角空间推理，并通过任务反馈强化学习联合优化中间表示的选择与使用。该工作迈向能自适应选择推理表征的物理世界模型。
papers.abstract_en: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce $Ψ$-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. These streams interleave images, text, and explicit representations of geometry and motion, all of which the model can generate and interpret through a shared token interface. $Ψ$-0.6 surpasses leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning, with further gains from reasoning through geometric intermediates. It also supports counterfactual simulation: generating and interpreting imagined scenes to determine, for example, whether moving an object would obstruct a pathway. Reinforcement learning from task feedback jointly optimizes the selection, generation, and use of intermediate representations, improving visual question-answering accuracy with gains that transfer to unseen benchmarks. $Ψ$-0.6 offers a path toward adaptive physical reasoning -- not only predicting the physical world but also choosing the representations through which to reason.
